title: Build a ProductCard
prompt: Write `ProductCard({ name, price, salePrice, inStock, onAdd })` for a catalogue grid. Prices are in cents, and `formatPrice` is written for you. Show the name as a heading and the price in dollars. When `salePrice` is lower than `price`, show a “Sale” badge, then the sale price and the old price inside `<s>`. When `inStock` is false, show “Out of stock” and disable the “Add to cart” button; otherwise the button calls `onAdd`.
hints: Work the conditions out above the `return`: `const onSale = salePrice !== undefined && salePrice < price;` reads better than a long expression inside the JSX.
Use `&&` for the parts that are either there or not (the badge, “Out of stock”) and a ternary for the price, which is one thing or the other.
`<button type="button" disabled={!inStock} onClick={onAdd}>` covers the button, and a fragment, `<>{formatPrice(salePrice)} <s>{formatPrice(price)}</s></>`, puts the two prices side by side.

title: Render a list with every state
prompt: Write `PeopleList({ status, people, query })` for a team directory. While `status` is `"loading"`, show “Loading people…” with `role="status"`; for `"error"`, show “Could not load people. Try again later.” with `role="alert"`. Otherwise show the people whose name contains `query` (trimmed, ignoring case) in a list, as “Asha Rao (Engineer)”, after a count: “1 person” or “3 people”. With no matches, show “No one matches “zed”.”, or “No people yet.” when there is no query. Give each item a stable key.
hints: Start with one early return for each of the loading and error states. The rest of the function then only deals with a loaded list.
Filter with `person.name.toLowerCase().includes(search.toLowerCase())`, where `search` is the trimmed query, and handle an empty result before the `return` that renders the list.
Use `key={person.id}` on the `<li>`: the index would keep a person’s element in the same place when the list is reordered, and one of the tests reorders it.

title: Build a quantity picker
prompt: Write `QuantityPicker({ min = 1, max = 10, initial = min, onChange })`: a “−” button, the quantity in an `<output>`, and a “+” button, inside a `<fieldset>` with the legend “Quantity”. Give the buttons the accessible names “Decrease” and “Increase” with `aria-label`. Each click changes the quantity by one, never past `min` or `max`, and each button is disabled at its limit. Every change calls `onChange` with the new quantity, and each picker on the page keeps its own quantity.
hints: Keep the quantity in state with `useState(initial)`. The disabled states are derived from it during render, so they need no state of their own.
Write one handler, `change(by)`, that works out the next value with `Math.min(max, Math.max(min, quantity + by))`, sets it and calls `onChange`.
Call `onChange?.(next)` in the handler, not in an effect: the handler is where you know the quantity changed and why. `onClick={() => change(-1)}` and `onClick={() => change(1)}` wire it up.

title: Fetch in an effect, without races
prompt: Write `UserCard({ userId })`. It fetches `/api/users/<userId>`, shows “Loading…” with `role="status"` until the answer arrives, then the user’s `name` in an `<h2>`. If the response is not ok, it shows “Could not load user 9.” (with the id) and `role="alert"`. When `userId` changes, or the card leaves the page, it cancels its request with an `AbortController`, so an old answer can never replace a newer one.
hints: Keep the whole request in one state value, such as `{ status: "loading" }`, `{ status: "success", user }` or `{ status: "error" }`, and render one early return per status.
In `useEffect(() => { … }, [userId])`, create an `AbortController`, pass `{ signal: controller.signal }` to `fetch`, and return `() => controller.abort()` as the cleanup.
An aborted fetch rejects with an error named `AbortError`. Ignore it in your `catch`, because it means a newer request (or unmounting) replaced this one, not that something failed.

title: Write useLocalStorage
prompt: Write `useLocalStorage(key, initialValue)`. It works like `useState`: it returns `[value, setValue]`, and `setValue` takes a value or an updater function. The first value is read from `localStorage` (as JSON) once, on the first render, falling back to `initialValue` when the key is missing or its text is not valid JSON. Every change is saved back under `key` as JSON.
hints: Start from `useState`: the hook returns exactly what `useState` returns, so the updater form comes for free.
Pass a function to `useState`, `useState(() => read(key, initialValue))`, so storage is read on the first render only. Wrap `JSON.parse` in `try`/`catch` to fall back on bad text.
Save in an effect: `useEffect(() => { localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value)); }, [key, value]);`.
